why_this_file_exists: The gate ratchet needs a list of unproven gates, each with a reason and a
slot. That list changes every time a gate closes — which made it a
recurring edit to tools/label_gates.py, and the repository's own churn
guard was right to object: a source file edited once per closed gate is a
file whose data does not belong in it.
So the backlog is data with ONE authority, and closing a gate edits this
file instead of the checker. The checker's logic stops changing entirely.

categories.blocked: something external prevents the attempt: a device, an arm64 host, an integration nobody has done yet.
categories.in_flight: the current run closes it. False the moment the run finishes, so entries must leave.
categories.measured_below: it WAS attempted and the number came up short. Added 2026-08-17, on Fable 5's adjudication, because the other two categories both lie about this state: in_flight implies pending work nobody owns, and blocked implies the attempt could not be made. The name is self-refuting against both misreadings — 'measured' rules out 'never attempted', 'below' rules out 'passed'. An empty slot is honest here; a fabricated owner is not.

blocked_history.4a: CLOSED 2026-08-18. Both halves of the blocker ended on the same night. The module: BoringSSL at the pinned commit b0760837 cross-built for the device, reached through a small C shim in the app's own pod (packages/pt_transport_darwin/ios/Sources/pt_shim.c) with bindings generated by ffigen — nothing vendored, the archives referenced where they were built. The peer: the same library's own command-line server, started locally with a configuration whose public name differs from the name asked for (tools/t2/step5_helper.sh). The measurement: the cabled phone answered `applied`, meaning the peer HONOURED the configuration rather than merely completing an exchange — the near-miss `ignored` is a separate outcome precisely so it cannot pass as success. Recorded in docs/evidence/step6_probe_answer.txt and held to its words by packages/adaptive_transport/test/ticket4_device_probe_test.dart. Worth keeping: the first device run answered `unreachable` against a wired LAN address the phone had no path to; the working route was the USB bridge at 192.168.2.1, which tools/t2/usb_peer.sh already knew about. A capability measurement can fail for network reasons, and the evidence names the route for exactly that reason.
